html:
In 1918 the new Azerbaijan Democratic Republic gave women the right to vote, the first Muslim majority country to do so. It came earlier than in Britain, France or the United States.

The republic was founded in May 1918 as the Russian Empire fell apart after the Russian Revolution. Its leaders, such as Mammad Amin Rasulzade, wanted a secular, democratic state for the Muslim Turkic people of the south Caucasus, with its capital at Baku, the oil city. They gave equal voting rights to all adult citizens, men and women, regardless of religion or ethnic group.

The republic lasted less than two years. In April 1920 the Red Army invaded, and Azerbaijan became a Soviet republic. Soviet law also gave women the vote, but in a one party state.

The 1918 law is remembered as an early step in the Muslim world. Turkish women won the vote in 1934, and women in many other Muslim countries only decades later.
sum: In 1918 the new Azerbaijan Democratic Republic gave women the right to vote, the first Muslim majority country to do so. It came earlier than in Britain, France or the United States.
